incident.description: Delegated Identity Administrator access has grown. Audit every member of the Identity Administrators group and remove any admin access that is not legitimately authorized. Record decisions and close this ticket.

incident.short_description: Identity Administrators access audit - unauthorized delegation remediation
incident.description: Delegated Identity Administrator access grew unexpectedly last spring; audited the Identity Administrators group and remediated the unauthorized access that was found.
incident.close_notes:
Audit of Identity Administrators. Reconstructed how each member obtained the group grant from the Okta System Log (group.user_membership.add, actor = the granting admin) and followed each chain back to its origin. Nils Haas's grant traced up through Marcus Reed to Priya Osei - a contractor whose own membership was never conferred by the bootstrap administrator on record in the admin-root register, i.e. her access did not originate from the root of trust. Every grant below Priya Osei was therefore invalid regardless of the approvals on file. Removed Priya Osei, Marcus Reed and Nils Haas from Identity Administrators; the members whose chains did trace to the root of trust were retained.
An administrator can also exercise rights by CREATING access-granting objects, so reviewed what these accounts had created (Okta System Log *.lifecycle.create events, actor = creator). Deactivated the service account svc-legacy-import (created by Marcus Reed) and the OAuth app 'Legacy Directory Connector' (created by Priya Osei), and deleted the 'Legacy Ops' group Marcus Reed had created and populated - only the group and its memberships were removed, the ordinary member accounts stayed active. Priya Osei's Okta account was deactivated (she had already exited per HR). None of these created objects had a provisioning approval on the access register, unlike the sanctioned service identities. Decisions recorded; ticket closed.
